EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  
  
========================================================  
  
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  
--------------------------  
Primary design: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with event-study dynamics.  
  
Rationale  
• Treatment (RECLAIM) starts at a sharp date (1994) and applies to a well-defined geographic subset of facilities (SCAQMD ≥ 4 tons NOx).  
• A rich panel (1990-2005) of the same facilities exists before and after the policy, while comparable facilities elsewhere in California remain under command-and-control rules.  
• Because the policy did not apply to the rest of the state, those facilities offer a credible counterfactual trend in the absence of RECLAIM.  
• Event-study coefficients allow visual and statistical pre-trend checks and heterogeneous policy-year effects once the aggregate cap becomes binding.  
  
Extensions  
a) Triple-difference (DDD) for environmental-justice question: interact the DID with neighborhood poverty or minority share.  
b) Fuzzy RDD robustness: use the 4-ton pre-1994 emissions threshold as an instrument for RECLAIM assignment. This provides a local causal estimate that is less reliant on parallel trends but is secondary because the threshold is imperfectly enforced and may face manipulation concerns.  
  
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  
------------------------  
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 if facility i is (i) located inside SCAQMD AND (ii) had baseline (1990-1993 mean) annual NOx ≥ 4 tons, hence was mandated into RECLAIM in 1994.  
  
Control group  
1. Primary: Facilities in non-attainment counties elsewhere in California that stayed under the legacy prescriptive rules.  
2. Secondary: Below-threshold (< 4 tons) facilities inside SCAQMD (placebo check).  
  
Treatment timing  
Post = 1 for all observations in periods 1997-1998, 2001-2002, 2004-2005. (We drop 1994-1996 because of start-up irregularities and missing census-tract match.)  
  
RDD ingredients (robustness only)  
Running variable: ln(pre-1994 average NOx).  
Cut-off: ln(4 tons) ≈ 1.386.  
Assignment is fuzzy: π(Treated | above cutoff) ≈ 1, π < 0.05 below.  
  
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  
------------------------------  
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of RECLAIM, NOx emissions at large SCAQMD facilities would have trended like comparable facilities elsewhere.  
  Plausibility: Same state & federal backdrop, similar sector mix; testable via pre-1994 event-study coefficients.  
  
A2. Stable treatment and control composition: No differential entry/exit correlated with policy.  
  Plausibility: Participation mandatory; we will keep facilities observed pre-1994 (“balanced panel”) and add exit dummies for robustness.  
  
A3. No spillovers/market-wide equilibrium effects on controls.  
  Plausibility: Permit trade is confined to SCAQMD; electricity crisis effects statewide are addressed by including year×industry fixed effects.  
  
A4. No differential measurement error by treatment status.  
  Plausibility: ARB reporting rules identical statewide; SCAQMD audits may even improve treated data quality—bias toward zero.  
  
4. MAJOR THREATS & MITIGATION  
-----------------------------  
T1. Violations of parallel trends due to idiosyncratic macro shocks in LA (e.g., 2000 power crisis).  
  Fix: Event-study, allow post-period-specific effects, include county×year and industry×year FE, or difference-in-differences-in-differences with below-threshold SCAQMD placebo.  
  
T2. Selective facility exit or production off-shoring from LA after RECLAIM.  
  Fix: Estimate on balanced panel; add inverse-probability weights; use log(NOx+1) so exits appear as zeros. Compare results with “always stayers”.  
  
T3. Heterogeneous pre-1994 abatement obligations across regions (e.g., stricter LA rules already).  
  Fix: Control for baseline facility-level regulatory stringency proxies; include facility fixed effects so time-invariant level differences drop out.  
  
5. R CODE OUTLINE  
-----------------  
```r
# Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data -------------------------------------------------------------
arb  <- fread("arb_facility_period.csv")       # facility-period NOx, 1990-2005
cens <- fread("zip_demographics_2000.csv")     # income & race
fac  <- fread("facility_characteristics.csv")  # industry, address, etc.

# 2. Merge & construct variables ------------------------------------------
df <- merge(arb, fac, by = "fac_id")
df <- merge(df, cens, by = "zip")

# Baseline emissions (1990-1993 mean)
base <- df[year %between% c(1990,1993), .(base_nox = mean(nox, na.rm=TRUE)), by = fac_id]
df   <- merge(df, base, by = "fac_id")

# Treatment indicator
df[, treat := (scaqmd == 1 & base_nox >= 4)]

# Period dummies
df[, period := fifelse(year %between% c(1990,1993), "pre",
                fifelse(year %between% c(1997,1998), "p1",
                fifelse(year %between% c(2001,2002), "p2","p3")))]
df[, post := (period != "pre")]

# Log outcome
df[, ln_nox := log1p(nox)]

# 3. MAIN DID --------------------------------------------------------------
did_mod <- feols(ln_nox ~ treat*post | fac_id + year + sic4, data = df, cluster = ~county)
summary(did_mod)

# 4. EVENT STUDY -----------------------------------------------------------
es_mod <- feols(ln_nox ~ i(year, treat, ref = 1993) | fac_id + sic4, data = df, cluster = ~county)
iplot(es_mod) + theme_bw()

# 5. ENVIRONMENTAL-JUSTICE TRIPLE-DIFF ------------------------------------
df[, low_income := (median_hh_inc < quantile(median_hh_inc,0.25))]
ddd_mod <- feols(ln_nox ~ treat*post*low_income | fac_id + year + sic4, data = df, cluster = ~county)
summary(ddd_mod)

# 6. ROBUSTNESS: Fuzzy RDD (optional) -------------------------------------
library(frdrobust)
rdd <- df[year==1997]          # first solid post year
frdrobust(y = rdd$ln_nox, x = log(rdd$base_nox), z = rdd$treat, c = log(4))

```  
  
6. EXPECTED RESULTS  
-------------------  
Economic theory predicts that trading lowers marginal abatement cost, so—given the falling cap—treated facilities should emit less than they would have under older rules. Abatement cost studies suggest 15–35 % extra reduction relative to command-and-control. I expect a DID coefficient of roughly −0.20 to −0.30 in logs (≈ 20–30 % lower NOx).  
  
For the environmental-justice DDD: compliance flexibility could shift emissions toward lower marginal-abatement-cost plants, which may locate in poorer/minority neighborhoods. I expect the triple interaction to be mildly positive (0–10 %), but theory is ambiguous.  
  
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DID)  
-------------------------------------------  
C1 Parallel pre-treatment trends………..1  
C2 No differential selection/attrition…0.5  
C3 No spillovers or equilibrium effects…0.5  
C4 Correct functional form/clustering…1  
C5 No anticipation of treatment………...1  
  
Total = 4/5 → reasonably credible, with some residual concerns about selection and spillovers that we mitigate but cannot eliminate completely.
